jobs.description:
BUSINESS OPERATIONS MANAGER
Full-Time | In-Person | Downtown Chicago

Performance AI is hiring a Business Operations Manager to build the operating foundation required to scale a growing enterprise AI company.

This is not a traditional administrative or maintenance role. You will work closely with the COO and CEO to turn leadership priorities into accountable plans, establish company-wide operating discipline, and ensure that important commitments do not fall through the cracks.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

• Base salary: $90,000–$100,000
• Annual performance bonus: Up to 10% of base salary
• Health benefits
• 401(k)
• Paid time off and paid sick leave
• Company-paid gym membership
• No Visa sponsorships available.

This is a full-time, in-person position at Performance AI’s office in Prudential Tower in downtown Chicago.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

You will build and manage the systems that create visibility, accountability, and reliable execution across the company.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Establishing the company’s operating cadence, including leadership meetings, quarterly priorities, decision logs, KPI reviews, and action tracking.
• Translating strategic priorities into clear plans with owners, deadlines, milestones, dependencies, and risks.
• Building company-wide dashboards, executive reports, operating procedures, and accountability systems.
• Managing cross-functional initiatives and escalating blockers before they affect customers, revenue, compliance, or delivery.
• Coordinating employee onboarding, offboarding, payroll inputs, benefits administration, background checks, equipment, access, and documentation.
• Supporting SOC 2, HIPAA, privacy, security, and customer compliance programs through evidence collection, remediation tracking, and audit readiness.
• Managing contract workflows, vendor onboarding, renewals, insurance records, procurement controls, and corporate documentation.
• Coordinating invoicing, accounts receivable, vendor payments, financial reporting inputs, and external accounting providers.
• Creating consistent sales-to-implementation handoffs, customer onboarding plans, status reporting, training coordination, launch readiness, and acceptance tracking.

The role is approximately:
• 50% company operations and cross-functional execution
• 35% people, compliance, vendor, and corporate operations
• 15% customer implementation operations

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You should have:

• At least 5 years of relevant experience in business operations, program management, corporate operations, implementation operations, or a related field.
• Demonstrated experience building or materially improving operating processes—not simply administering existing ones.
• Strong project-management and cross-functional execution skills.
• The ability to establish accountability across peers and senior stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
• Excellent written communication, documentation, reporting, and executive-summary skills.
• Strong judgment regarding what to handle independently, what requires consultation, and what must be escalated.
• The discretion required to work with employee, customer, financial, legal, security, and company-confidential information.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

Experience in one or more of the following areas is strongly preferred:

• B2B technology, enterprise software, healthcare technology, financial services, or another regulated industry.
• SOC 2, HIPAA, privacy, security, or enterprise customer compliance.
• Enterprise customer onboarding, implementation, professional services, or delivery operations.
• Contract administration, procurement, vendor due diligence, insurance, or corporate records.
• Payroll, billing, accounts receivable, or month-end coordination.
• Working directly with founders and senior executives.

YOU WILL SUCCEED HERE IF YOU

• Take ownership and consistently close loops.
• Bring structure to fast-moving situations without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.
• Challenge unclear ownership, unrealistic deadlines, and hidden risks directly and professionally.
• Identify problems early and recommend practical solutions.
• Move comfortably between strategy and detailed execution.
• Prefer measurable results, documented decisions, and clear accountability over activity for its own sake.
• Keep leadership informed before problems become surprises.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within your first 90 days, you will be expected to:

• Establish a company-wide priority tracker and leadership operating cadence.
• Create a master calendar of critical corporate, HR, legal, compliance, insurance, vendor, and customer obligations.
• Centralize contracts, vendor records, policies, insurance documents, and corporate records.
• Standardize employee onboarding and offboarding.
• Implement a compliance and operational risk register.
• Establish a repeatable sales-to-implementation handoff and customer onboarding process.
• Present a prioritized 12-month business operations roadmap.

WHY JOIN PERFORMANCE AI

You will have the opportunity to:

• Build the operating foundation of a growing enterprise AI company.
• Work directly with the COO and CEO on issues affecting customers, revenue, compliance, and scale.
• Shape how the company plans, communicates, documents decisions, and executes.
• Operate at the intersection of AI, enterprise technology, regulated industries, and business transformation.
• Grow toward a Director of Business Operations position as the company scales and your performance supports the expansion.

LOCATION REQUIREMENT

Candidates must currently live within commuting distance of downtown Chicago or independently relocate before their start date. Relocation assistance is not available.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYMENT

Performance AI is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Ally and Your Career

Ally Financial only succeeds when its people do - and that’s more than some cliché people put on job postings. We love this stuff! We see our people as, well, people - with interests, families, friends, dreams, and causes that are all important to them. Our focus is on the health and safety of our teammates as well as work-life balance and diversity and inclusion. From generous benefits to a variety of employee resource groups, we strive to build paths that encourage employees to stretch themselves professionally. We want to help you grow, develop, and learn new things. You’re constantly evolving, so shouldn’t your opportunities be, too?

Work Schedule:
Ally designates roles as (1) fully on-site, (2) hybrid, or (3) fully remote. Hybrid roles are generally expected to be in the office a certain number of days per week as indicated by your manager. Your hiring manager will discuss this role's specific work requirements with you during the hiring process. All work requirements are subject to change at any time based on leader discretion and/or business need.

The Opportunity

Ally is seeking a Physical Security Event & Travel Risk Intelligence Manager to join our Physical Security organization to support delivering proactive and real-time intelligence for high-visibility Ally sponsored events and executive engagements.

In this role, you will partner closely with Travel & Entertainment, Marketing, Executive Protection, and Physical Security Intelligence teams to assess risk, monitor threats, and ensure the safety of employees and leadership during corporate events. You will be responsible for conducting threat intelligence analysis, supporting event planning through risk assessments, and developing emergency action plans (EAPs) that address employee and executive exposure.

This role also plays a critical role in supporting Executive Protection, providing ongoing intelligence and situational awareness for the CEO and other executives during Ally sponsored events, travel, and public-facing activities.

This is a 24/7, event-driven role that requires flexibility to support evolving threats and real-time operational needs. Candidates must be willing to work non-traditional hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, and respond to live security or life safety incidents as they arise.

As the Physical Security Event & Travel Risk Intelligence Manager, you will lead intelligence efforts tied to corporate and executive events, ensuring risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated through proactive planning and real-time support.

The Work Itself

Conduct intelligence-driven risk assessments for corporate events, sponsored events, and employee gatherings
Partner with Event, Marketing and Executive Protection teams to perform due diligence on event locations, environments, and attendee exposure
Monitor open-source intelligence (OSINT), social media, and threat intelligence feeds for emerging risks that could impact events
Develop and maintain event-specific Emergency Action Plans (EAPs), ensuring alignment with security and crisis management protocols
Partner with Executive Protection to provide threat intelligence and situational awareness for CEO and executive exposure during events and engagements
Provide real-time monitoring, reporting, and escalation support during live events, including response to active security or life safety incidents
Investigate and assess potential threats using multiple data sources and intelligence tools
Produce clear, concise intelligence risk products
Collaborate with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment on risk posture and response planning
Build dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility to leadership
Translate data into insights and recommendations for operational improvement
Continuously evolve threat detection, monitoring practices, and reporting standards
Drive refinement of monitoring strategies to improve detection accuracy and reduce noise
Ensure consistency in decision-making, escalation, and reporting quality

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in security studies, criminal justice, international relations, homeland security or related discipline or equivalent military/law enforcement experience
Proficiency in protective intelligence, event security planning, risk assessments, executive protection support, crisis management, travel risk management, or geopolitical analysis
Proven ability to synthesize large volumes of information into actionable intelligence and concise reporting
Demonstrated ability to make independent decisions in fast-paced, ambiguous situations to assess threats and risks in dynamic environments
Experience supporting executive protection programs, corporate sponsored events, or other large-scale events
Background building and managing physical security programs
Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills across technical and non-technical teams
Familiarity with incident response, crisis management, and physical security practices
Experience utilizing threat intelligence monitoring tools
Strong OSINT monitoring capabilities, threat assessment, travel risk analysis, and the ability to identify and triage emerging threats and produce actionable intelligence products
Excellent verbal & written communication skills for executive-level communication
Experience working with cross-functional teams and leaders across many levels of management
Working independently in an unstructured environment; developing structure and clarity around the ambiguous by taking a concept and developing ideas/about solutions to achieve progress
Navigating through complex collaborative initiatives while aligning
Strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, attention to detail, source validation skills, situational awareness, and the ability to remain calm under pressure
Proven ability developing trusted partnerships in both public & private sectors
Proficiency in Microsoft office products

Additional Requirements For All Physical Security Roles

Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, which may include movement throughout company facilities, conducting security assessments, supporting operational activities, participating in emergency response procedures, and carrying out assigned security responsibilities.
Ability to recognize, assess, document, escalate, and appropriately respond to security incidents, safety concerns, emergencies, disruptions, or unauthorized access events using sound judgment, established procedures, and effective communication.
Ability to successfully obtain, maintain, and demonstrate proficiency in required security, safety, emergency response, compliance, or other job-related training, certifications, and qualifications applicable to the position.

Ability to meet applicable job-related lifting requirements, including repetitive lifting where required by the role, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Minimum Qualifications

7+ years of relevant experience or equivalent combination of education and experience
High school Diploma or GED equivalent

How We'll Have Your Back

Ally's compensation program offers market-competitive base pay and pay-for-performance incentives (bonuses) based on achieving personal and company goals. Our Total Rewards program includes industry-leading compensation and benefits plus additional incentives that are designed to meet your needs and those of your family so you can get the most out of your career and your life, including:

Program starts at 20 paid time off days in addition to 11 paid holidays and 8 hours of volunteer time off yearly (time off days are prorated based on start date and program varies based on full or part-time status and management level).

plan for the near and long term with an industry-leading 401K retirement savings plan with matching and company contributions, student loan pay downs and 529 educational save up assistance programs, tuition reimbursement, employee stock purchase plan, and financial learning center and financial coach access.

flexible health and insurance options including medical, dental and vision, employee, spouse and child life insurance, short- and long-term disability, pre-tax Health Savings Account with employer contributions, Healthcare FSA, critical illness, accident & hospital indemnity insurance, and a total well-being program that helps you and your family stay on track physically, socially, emotionally, and financially.

adoption, surrogacy and fertility assistance as well as paid parental and caregiver leave, Dependent Day Care FSA back-up child and adult/elder care days and childcare discounts.

other benefits including Mentally Fit Employee Assistance Program, subsidized and discounted Weight Watchers® program and other employee discount programs.

depending on the role for which you are considered, you may be eligible for travel allowances, relocation assistance, a signing bonus and/or equity.

jobs.title: Investigations Manager
jobs.description:
Job Introduction

Role Purpose

The Fraud and Financial Crime Investigations Manager is responsible for identifying and investigating suspected criminal, fraudulent and dishonest activity affecting the business, its customers and colleagues.

The role will manage investigations from initial identification through to conclusion, seeking, gathering and assessing evidence, identifying patterns of offending, conducting interviews where appropriate and producing clear investigation reports. The Investigations Manager will work closely with store teams, Loss Prevention, Employee Relations and other internal stakeholders, as well as external agencies where required.

A key focus of the position is moving beyond individual incidents to identify repeat offenders, organised activity, emerging crime trends and weaknesses in processes or controls that may expose the business to further loss.

Key Responsibilities

Investigations

Conduct thorough investigations into suspected internal and external retail crime, fraud and dishonest activity which may include theft and attempted theft, employee dishonesty and internal fraud, refund, return and exchange abuse, discount, loyalty or promotional abuse and abuse of company processes or systems for financial gain
Manage investigations from initial allegation or intelligence through to conclusion
Review available evidence including CCTV, transaction records, till activity, payment information, access records, delivery information and relevant business records
Establish clear investigation timelines and identify links between incidents, individuals, transactions and locations
Conduct investigative interviews and obtain relevant accounts or statements in line with company procedures
Maintain clear, accurate and professional investigation records
Produce concise investigation reports setting out the evidence, findings and recommended next steps
Ensure investigations are proportionate, objective and evidence led

Evidence & Case Management

Gather, assess and preserve evidence appropriately
Maintain comprehensive investigation files and clear audit trails
Ensure case records accurately document investigative decisions and actions
Handle sensitive information with appropriate confidentiality
Prepare investigation material suitable for internal disciplinary or criminal justice processes where required
Support requests for evidence from law enforcement or other authorised external bodies in accordance with company procedures

Intelligence & Crime Prevention

Use internal systems to identify suspicious transactions and behaviour that require further investigation
Identify repeat offenders, linked incidents and emerging methods of offending
Analyse investigation information to identify trends, vulnerabilities and potential control weaknesses
Share relevant intelligence with operational teams and other appropriate stakeholders
Identify opportunities to prevent recurrence and recommend improvements to processes or controls

Stakeholder & External Partnership

Build effective working relationships with store management, Loss Prevention, Employee Relations, Legal, Security and operational teams
Liaise professionally with police and other relevant external agencies where appropriate.
Provide investigative advice and guidance to colleagues
Communicate complex investigation findings clearly to both operational and senior stakeholders
Support the business in understanding emerging retail crime and fraud risks through training and communication

The ideal candidate

Essential

Experience in retail investigations, loss prevention, fraud investigation, security, law enforcement or a comparable investigative environment
Strong investigative and analytical skills
Ability to assess information objectively and distinguish evidence from assumption
Strong attention to detail and ability to identify connections across multiple incidents or data sources
Experience producing clear written investigation reports
Confident communication and interviewing skills, Wicklander-Zulawski trained an advantage
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information appropriately
Strong organisational and case-management skills
Ability to manage multiple investigations and competing priorities
Sound judgement and confidence when making evidence-based recommendations

Desirable

Experience investigating internal fraud or employee dishonesty
Experience of investigations involving high-value retail environments
Knowledge of payment fraud, refund abuse, organised retail crime or ecommerce fraud
Experience working with CCTV and transaction-monitoring data
Experience liaising with police or other external agencies, including writing of MG11s and exhibiting of appropriate evidence
Relevant investigative, fraud, security or financial crime qualification

Open to some regional travel, specifically to our stores in Birmingham and Manchester.

jobs.title: Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

INTELLIGENCE ANALYST

SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies, including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we attract foreign and domestic adversaries intent on impeding our progress and stealing our technology. The work we do will safeguard mankind as we become an interplanetary species.

You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the security of personnel, global assets, and operations at SpaceX. You will use various collection methods and platforms to explore data, identify critical information, build queries, and assess risk to produce actional insights that drive informed business decisions.

Responsibilities

Conduct in-depth research, evaluation, analysis, integration, and interpretation of information sourced from various open sources.
Produce high-quality intelligence products on a daily, weekly, and monthly cadence, including data visualization, briefings, and analytic reports.
Perform enhanced due diligence on companies and people within established tradecraft standards.
Utilize data aggregators and OSINT tools to conduct open-source research, and leverage social media platforms, deep web, dark web, and breach data to identify hidden connections.
Identify emerging risks to the company, our technology, and people and quickly synthesize information to share with relevant stakeholders.
Communicate findings effectively and accurately to team members, leadership, and relevant stakeholders.
Facilitate information sharing by fostering relationships and partnering with internal stakeholders as well as external local and federal law enforcement.
Conduct intelligence analysis, threat assessments, and investigations on persons, companies, and organizations of interest.
Develop risk mitigation strategies to address identified and work with internal teams to implement them.
Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case file and intelligence reports.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in intelligence analysis, enhanced due diligence (EDD), third party risk management (TPRM), supply chain risk management (SCRM), and/or investigations; OR 4+ years of professional experience in the aforementioned areas in lieu of a degree.

Preferred Skills And Experience

2+ years of all-source intelligence experience in the military, intelligence community, federal law enforcement, or in the private sector at a high-tech company and/or US Government contractor.
Familiarity with trade compliance regulations and restrictions, including export controls (ITAR, EAR, etc.) and import controls.
Experience supporting trade compliance and/or supply chain teams and implementing TPRM and Denied Party Screening programs.
Experience with open-source intelligence gathering tools/techniques for application/web-based social media platforms including web scraping, data parsing, and metadata extraction.
Experience performing business process automation, constructing data pipelines, building dashboards, and developing robust queries and AI prompts.
Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate with security and engineering teams on technical topics. This includes maintaining conceptual understandings of foundational topics related to data structures, databases, APIs, network infrastructure, and access controls.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze large data sets and draw actionable insights.
Knowledge of analytic tradecraft standards, source validation, and disinformation detection.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise research reports and briefings for a wide variety of internal and external audiences.
Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment in a fast-paced, high-tech environment.
Highly organized with a strong attention to detail.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.
High degree of emotional intelligence and maturity.
Strong critical thinking skills and a solutions-oriented mindset.

Additional Requirements

Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations.
Must be willing to travel ad hoc, although only minimal travel is expected at this time.
Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment.

Compensation And Benefits

Pay Range:

Level 1: $85,000 - $110,000

Level 2: $100,000 - $135,000

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

Itar Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.
1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Department Overview

The Market Intelligence function is a dedicated strategic team within the Chief Marketing Organization designed to embed evidence-based insights into our global strategy. By synthesizing high-fidelity research, this team optimizes our market positioning and resource allocation to drive long-term, sustainable growth in a dynamic landscape.

jobs.title: AI Data Analyst - Merchant Acquisition
jobs.description:
About Us

We are an established Independent Sales Organization with seven years of experience in the credit-card-processing and merchant-services industry. We understand how merchants evaluate processors, why they consider switching, the objections they raise and the factors that ultimately drive conversion.

We are building a proprietary, AI-driven lead-intelligence platform to identify and prioritize merchants most likely to become customers. Our goal is to combine our industry knowledge, current sales-call recordings, operational information and external business data into a system that makes prospecting more scientific, targeted and measurable.

We are seeking an entrepreneurial data-science leader to design and lead this initiative from research and prototype development through prospective testing and commercialization.

The Opportunity

This is not a conventional data-science position in which a completed dataset and predefined model are handed to you. You will help determine what data matters, how it should be collected and labeled, and how qualitative sales intelligence can be transformed into quantitative predictions.

Because our historical labeled data is limited, the initial work will include analyzing current sales-call recordings, interviewing members of our sales organization and identifying the characteristics, circumstances and behaviors associated with merchants who are receptive to switching processors.

The successful candidate will build an initial lead-scoring methodology, test it against real-world sales results and continuously improve it as new outcome data is generated.

This is a founding-level opportunity with salary and equity participation in the resulting platform. The right candidate will have substantial autonomy and the opportunity to create a potentially valuable commercial product within an established operating business.

Responsibilities

Develop the overall research, data and AI strategy for a proprietary merchant lead-intelligence platform.
Analyze recorded sales conversations using transcription, natural-language processing, large language models and human-reviewed qualitative research.
Create a structured framework for extracting relevant information from calls, including merchant characteristics, processing concerns, switching triggers, objections, urgency, decision-maker engagement and sales outcomes.
Interview sales representatives and company leadership to capture domain knowledge that may not appear in existing structured data.
Design reliable labeling and quality-control procedures for call transcripts and sales outcomes.
Identify the signals most likely to predict meaningful sales progression, including statement submissions, follow-up meetings, proposals and signed merchant accounts.
Develop an initial transparent, rules-based scoring model suitable for use while labeled data remains limited.
Progressively develop statistical and machine-learning models as sufficient prospective data becomes available.
Identify and evaluate external data sources that could reveal merchant size, growth, industry, number of locations, technology, ownership changes, hiring activity and other relevant characteristics.
Connect internal conversation insights to externally observable business signals that can be used to identify new prospects.
Design controlled sales experiments comparing AI-selected leads with leads selected through our existing process.
Establish appropriate performance metrics, including conversion lift, precision among top-ranked leads, customer-acquisition cost and expected merchant profitability.
Work with sales leadership to integrate lead recommendations into the company’s existing workflow.
Build or manage the development of an initial working prototype and subsequent production platform.
Develop appropriate documentation, data-governance practices and safeguards for sensitive sales and merchant information.
Help evaluate and recruit additional data, engineering or research talent as the project grows.
Communicate findings and recommendations clearly to business leadership and nontechnical sales personnel.

Required Qualifications

Advanced training or equivalent professional experience in data science, applied statistics, machine learning, computer science, econometrics, quantitative marketing or a closely related field.
Demonstrated experience with predictive modeling, propensity modeling, lead scoring, customer analytics or another classification/ranking problem.
Strong Python and SQL capabilities.
Experience working with unstructured text, call transcripts, conversation analytics or natural-language processing.
Familiarity with large language models and their use in structured information extraction, classification and research workflows.
Ability to work effectively with limited historical data and develop a disciplined data-collection and validation plan.
Understanding of experimental design, prospective validation, model evaluation and common problems such as data leakage, overfitting and selection bias.
Ability to combine qualitative business research with quantitative analysis.
Strong product judgment and an interest in building a commercial platform, not merely producing an academic model or research report.
Ability to work independently, define priorities and communicate directly with company leadership.
High standards for confidentiality, security and responsible handling of recorded conversations and merchant information.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in merchant acquiring, credit-card processing, payments, fintech, banking or financial services.
Experience analyzing B2B sales calls or developing sales-intelligence, revenue-operations or customer-acquisition systems.
Familiarity with merchant categories, processing statements, pricing structures, interchange, chargebacks, point-of-sale systems and the reasons merchants change processors.
Experience with speech-to-text systems, embeddings, retrieval systems and LLM evaluation.
Experience combining internal company data with licensed or publicly available external business data.
Experience taking a data product from initial research through deployment and ongoing monitoring.
Previous startup, founding-team or entrepreneurial experience.
Experience managing technical contributors or outside development resources.

Initial Objectives

During the first several months, the successful candidate will be expected to:

Audit the information currently available, including sales-call recordings, CRM information and business outcomes.
Interview company leadership and high-performing sales representatives.
Develop a taxonomy for merchant needs, dissatisfaction, switching triggers, objections and levels of sales progression.
Build and validate an AI-assisted process for transcribing, reviewing and structuring sales conversations.
Produce an initial rules-based lead-scoring system based on qualitative and quantitative evidence.
Recommend external data sources and determine which observable merchant characteristics can support prospect identification.
Design a prospective experiment comparing prioritized leads with the company’s current lead-selection process.
Deliver a working prototype and a roadmap for developing a defensible production platform.

What Success Looks Like

Success Will Not Be Measured By Producing An Impressive Demonstration Or Using The Newest AI Technology. It Will Be Measured By Whether The System Consistently Helps Our Sales Organization

Reach more qualified decision-makers.
Identify merchants with genuine reasons to reconsider their current processor.
Obtain more processing statements and substantive follow-up meetings.
Generate more proposals from the same amount of sales activity.
Improve close rates and merchant profitability.
Explain why particular leads are being prioritized.
Learn and improve as additional sales outcomes are generated.

Why Join Us

Join an established ISO with seven years of merchant-services experience and real industry knowledge.
Lead a strategically important initiative with direct access to company decision-makers and sales personnel.
Build a proprietary AI and data product around an identifiable commercial need.
Receive a competitive salary together with meaningful equity participation.
Work remotely with substantial autonomy.
Have the opportunity to develop the project into a broader commercial platform.

Salary

Candidates will be paid a competitive salary based on experience. Expected pay range is $70-80,000 per year. This position is full time and eligible for full benefits package as well.

Company Description

OpenText is a leading Cloud and AI company that helps organizations worldwide grow, innovate, and operate more efficiently through trusted information management solutions. Founded in 1991 in Waterloo, OpenText has evolved from digitizing the Oxford English Dictionary into a global leader serving over 120,000 enterprise customers across 180 countries, including 98 of the top 100 global companies. The company offers a broad portfolio in Business AI, Business Clouds, and Business Technology, enabling customers to unlock the value of their information with AI, cloud, and security innovations. The GIS Cloud Security team helps secure 3000+ cloud accounts in AWS, Azure, GCP. OpenText is proudly AI-first, fostering a collaborative and inclusive culture where digital knowledge workers can thrive and drive forward-thinking solutions.

The Lead Cloud Security Analyst – CNAPP is a full-time, on-site role based in Ontario, Canada. This role is responsible for leading the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of cloud-native application protection platforms (CNAPP) across OpenText’s cloud environments. Day-to-day activities include assessing cloud security posture, analyzing threats and vulnerabilities, reviewing application and network security configurations, and coordinating incident response for cloud-based workloads. The analyst collaborates with engineering, DevOps, and security teams to embed security controls into cloud architectures, define secure coding and deployment practices, and ensure compliance with internal and external standards. The role also involves preparing detailed security reports, providing guidance on risk mitigation, and mentoring other team members on cloud security best practices and emerging threats.

Strong foundation in cybersecurity, including experience with cloud security frameworks, risk assessment, and threat modeling.
Expertise in application security, such as secure SDLC practices, code review for security issues, and protecting cloud-native applications and APIs.
Advanced analytical skills for interpreting complex security data, investigating incidents, and making evidence-based recommendations.

Experience with malware analysis or threat intelligence, including identifying malicious behaviors and supporting incident response activities.

Position Overview

SUMMARY (Basic Purpose of the Job):

The IT Security Analyst II independently owns and manages core information security programs, including third-party risk management (TPRM), Security Awareness Training, and Application Security Assessments. This role serves as a trusted resource for staff and leaders regarding information security policy implementation, interpretation, and compliance, and drafts and maintains information security policies, standards, and procedures. Building on the foundation of the IT Security Analyst I role, this position operates with greater autonomy, owns end-to-end programs and initiatives, and provides mentorship and guidance to less experienced team members. The position assesses and prioritizes information security and cybersecurity risk across the organization, facilitates compliance with regulatory requirements and information security policies, and develops and reports on information security metrics.

Minimum Requirements

Education:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience.

Experience:
Three years demonstrated experience in cybersecurity, GRC, vulnerability management, TPRM, or related roles, including experience gained as an IT Security Analyst I or in an equivalent role required. Working knowledge of NIST CSF, HIPAA, or other security/regulatory frameworks required. CompTIA Security+ required. One or more mid-level certifications such as CompTIA CySA+ or ISACA CRISC preferred (or equivalent). Progress toward or attainment of ISACA CISM, CISA, or ISC2 CISSP is a plus.

Knowledge and Skills:
Strong working knowledge of desktop, server, storage, virtualization, networking, and security technologies. Demonstrated ability to independently lead risk assessments, vendor risk reviews, and vulnerability remediation efforts, and to translate technical findings into business risk language for non-technical stakeholders.

Special Training:
A+, Network+, Security+, CySA+, CRISC, or other relevant IT security certifications are a plus.

Mental, Behavioral and Emotional Abilities:
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, exercise sound judgment on risk-based decisions, mentor junior staff, and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences under time-sensitive conditions.

Essential Functions

Owns and manages the third-party risk management (TPRM) program end-to-end, including vendor classification logic, risk scoring methodology, intake routing/workflows, assessment questionnaires, and reassessment tracking; serves as the primary point of contact for vendor risk questions across the organization.
Independently drives vendor risk assessments from initial outreach through closure, including follow-up with unresponsive vendors, review of vendor-submitted documentation, and escalation of high-risk or unresolved vendor relationships to leadership.
Administers the organization's enterprise phishing simulation program, including campaign design and scheduling, execution, data collection, results analysis, and reporting of metrics and trends to leadership.
Performs Application Security Assessments for new and existing software, evaluating security posture and providing risk-based recommendations to stakeholders.
Owns and manages the software request and review process, evaluating new software and vendor tools for security risk prior to approval and onboarding.
Provides broader support to overall GRC program strategy and planning, partnering with the IT Manager on initiatives such as multi-campaign phishing simulation roadmaps, TPRM process improvements, and team capacity/workload planning for a small, high-throughput GRC team.
Researches, drafts, and maintains information security policies, standards, procedures, and performs detailed policy reviews. Tracks and reports on remediation progress for regulatory and framework-based gap assessments (e.g., HIPAA Security Rule), maintaining a remediation tracker and coordinating with control owners to close identified gaps.
Develops and maintains security awareness training content for staff and management audiences, including designing and updating training presentation materials with current statistics and emerging threat topics.
Coordinates examinations by qualified security assessors for regulations and frameworks such as HIPAA and NIST, working with control owners and external assessors to ensure evidence requests are completed timely and accurately.
Monitors security alerts, analyzes incidents, and contributes to incident response activities in coordination with the Security Operations team and IT Manager.
Manages the exception review and approval process, ensuring exceptions are documented, risk-rated, and reviewed on schedule. Applies current threat intelligence and security trends to inform TPRM, awareness training, and policy work.
Collaborates closely with the IT Manager and Security Operations team on day-to-day operational challenges and contributes to effective, sustainable solutions as part of a small, high-throughput GRC team.
Mentors and provides guidance to IT Security Analyst I team members and other GRC support staff, including knowledge transfer, review of work products, and onboarding support; serves as a go-to resource for procedural and technical questions within the GRC team.
Maintains comprehensive documentation of TPRM activities, vendor assessments, security awareness training and phishing simulation activities, and policy review work.
Generates and analyzes regular reports on information security metrics (e.g., phishing simulation results, vendor assessment status, remediation tracking) for management review, identifying trends and improvement opportunities.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Senior Data Analyst – Strategic & Program Analytics

Location:
Dallas, TX | Hybrid or Remote
Compensation:
$100–140k Base Salary

A mission-driven organization in Dallas is looking for Senior Data Analysts
to join a growing Strategic Analytics function focused on using data to tackle some of the city's most complex social challenges.

This organization works at the intersection of data, public policy, healthcare, housing, education, criminal justice, and community programs
, partnering with public agencies and community organizations to turn evidence into action. The broader mission is ambitious and measurable: helping dramatically reduce child poverty across Dallas by improving how public resources and programs reach children and families.

These are not traditional reporting or dashboard-focused analyst positions. We're looking for people who can take broad, ambiguous real-world questions
, determine what can legitimately be answered with the available data, conduct rigorous analysis, and translate their findings into recommendations that leaders can actually act on.

The Opportunities

There are multiple openings across two types of Senior Data Analyst roles:

Senior Data Analyst – Strategy

You'll operate as a cross-functional analytical problem solver, working on questions that may come directly from city officials, agency leaders, foundations, and internal leadership.

One week you might be investigating where eligible families aren't accessing public benefits; another could involve understanding geographic gaps in healthcare access, patterns in school attendance, housing affordability, or public safety.

This role leans heavily into statistics, public and administrative data, and analytical judgment
. You'll need to understand not only how to perform an analysis, but whether the available data can actually support the conclusion someone wants to draw. The underlying JD specifically emphasizes regression, sampling and weighting, hypothesis testing, missing data, and understanding the limitations of estimates.

Senior Data Analyst – Program

You'll embed with a specific program area such as housing, maternal health, public safety, benefits delivery, or criminal justice
, becoming that team's dedicated analytics partner.

You'll learn the program's strategy, stakeholders, and recurring decisions, then use data to help the team understand what's happening, why it matters, and where resources or interventions may have the greatest impact.

Both roles involve working heavily with messy, real-world datasets
, with much of the information coming from publicly available sources and administrative data rather than perfectly structured internal systems.

What You'll Do:

Turn ambiguous stakeholder requests into clearly defined, answerable analytical questions.
Source, combine, clean, and analyze public, administrative, and internal datasets.
Evaluate data quality, missingness, sampling issues, outliers, margins of error, and other limitations before drawing conclusions.
Apply statistical methods such as regression, hypothesis testing, sampling, and weighting
where appropriate.
Identify confounding factors and clearly communicate what the data does and does not
support.
Build clean, reproducible analytical workflows using R, Python, Stata, or similar tools
.
Translate complex findings into concise recommendations, decision memos, and visuals for non-technical stakeholders.
Partner directly with program leaders, public agencies, and community stakeholders to influence resource allocation, program design, and strategy.
Use AI-assisted tools across research, coding, and QA while independently validating the methodology and final conclusions.

What We're Looking For:

3–4+ years of applied analytical experience
solving real-world business, policy, research, healthcare, consulting, or program-related problems.
Strong statistical foundations and the judgment to determine which analytical approach is appropriate — and when the data isn't strong enough to support a conclusion.
Hands-on experience working with messy, complex datasets
, ideally including public, administrative, healthcare, policy, demographic, or other real-world data.
Fluency in at least one analytical programming language such as R, Python, or Stata
.
Experience creating reproducible, well-documented analytical workflows.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly translating technical analysis for non-technical decision-makers.
A consultative mindset: you're comfortable receiving an unclear question, figuring out what the stakeholder actually needs to know, and independently determining how to answer it.

Nice to Have:

Experience in one or more of the following would be particularly valuable:
Program evaluation / impact evaluation • causal inference • quasi-experimental methods • health outcomes or HEOR • economic or quantitative consulting • public policy analytics • geographic/spatial analysis • demographic analysis • government or nonprofit analytics

Benefits include health, dental and vision insurance, retirement savings with employer match, generous PTO and holidays, and professional development support.

Career growth, your way: benefit from structured learning, certifications and clear development opportunities.

Global impact, local connections: work in an international environment while supporting local and regional initiatives.

How You’ll Contribute To Our Success

Participate in end-to-end data flow topics, from requirements gathering to the design and implementation of robust BI solutions.
Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into clear functional and technical specifications.
Collect and prepare data from various sources, ensuring data quality, consistency and reliability.

Your Skills

Must have

Bachelor’s degree in Business Intelligence, Data/Business Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related field.
6–8 years of proven experience in a Data Analyst, Data Engineer or similar role, with strong expertise in T-SQL and Microsoft SQL Server.
Solid experience with BI and reporting tools, especially Power BI (Power Query, DAX, row-level security) and SSRS (paginated reports).

Nice to have

Experience with SSIS and ETL/ELT workflows, as well as concepts such as Data Warehousing, Data Lakes and dimensional modelling (star/snowflake).
Exposure to Databricks and/or Azure services (e.g. Azure Data Factory, Synapse, SQL Database, Data Lake) or other cloud-based data platforms.
Master’s degree and/or relevant certifications in data or cloud technologies.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to quickly understand complex datasets and business contexts.
Structured, methodical and rigorous approach, with the ability to manage multiple tasks, priorities and deadlines.
Collaborative mindset and strong team spirit, with a willingness to share knowledge and support others.

IT Skills

Advanced T-SQL (complex queries, stored procedures, performance tuning, indexing and optimization).
Practical experience with data modelling and data analysis for BI solutions.
Hands-on experience with BI/ETL tools such as Power BI, SSRS and SSIS (or similar tools).

Ability to work fluently in English and French on a daily basis.

Participate in the development of reports, metrics, models, scorecards, and dashboards by gathering data and transforming it into stories and insights that drive business recommendations and decision-making.
Publish daily, weekly, and monthly reports accurately and on time
Build reports and dashboards in Microsoft Power BI, Analysis for Office, Bex, and other reporting tools
Build automated processes using scripting tools (i.e. Power Automate, Alteryx, SQL, Python, etc.)
Participate in hosted training sessions on how to use the various tools and reports created by the department
Generate load files for various systems, maintaining system accuracy

Perform ad hoc analysis using data from various systems and explain results of analysis to all levels of management
Create SOPs and maintain documentation for processes
Demonstrate continuous efforts to improve processes, increase data integrity, and provide quality customer service to our business partners.
Provide comprehensive analytical and fact-based reporting to support and/or identify opportunities to impact operational results, make changes to processes, and support strategic initiatives.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential functions.

Bachelor's Degree from an accredited four-year college or university in Accounting/Finance, Computer Science/Data Analytics, Business Management/Supply Chain or related field and 2+ years of relevant work experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.
Ability to build models using advanced features of Excel.
Relevant experience in Finance, preferably within Supply Chain/Manufacturing/Operations at a CPG.
Experience with Power BI / Tableau, Power Pivot, SAP, SAP Analysis for Office, BPC, Bex Query Designer or similar.
Experience in analyzing data within relational database systems such as MS Access, MS SQL Server, and MySQL.
Experience with ETL Tools such as Alteryx, Paxata, DataGuru or equivalent technologies, preferred.
Experience in programming language(s) such as Python, R, Javascript, etc., preferred.
Ability to quickly learn new technology and business logic.
Superior analytical and problem-solving skills with superb attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced and rapidly changing and ambiguous environment.
Ability to be respectful, approachable and team oriented while building strong working relationships and a positive work environment.

Company Description

Henry Ford Health partners with millions of people on their health journey, across Michigan and around the world. We offer a full continuum of services from primary and preventative care to complex and specialty care, health insurance, a full suite of home health offerings, virtual care, pharmacy, eye care and other health care retail. With former Ascension southeast Michigan and Flint region locations now part of our team, Henry Ford's care is available in 13 hospitals and hundreds of ambulatory care locations. Based in Detroit, Henry Ford is one of the nation's most respected academic medical centers and is leading the Future of Health: Detroit, a $3 billion investment anchored by a reimagined Henry Ford academic healthcare campus.

Job Description

The CQI Senior Registry Data Analyst serves as a technical and operational leader responsible for the design, development, implementation, and optimization of registry databases, data collection systems, websites, reports, and workflows that support quality improvement initiatives across Michigan. Working with limited supervision, this role partners with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the collection of accurate, high-quality data that drives improvements in patient care and outcomes.

This position serves as the subject matter expert for registry data collection processes, database functionality, reporting, and workflow design. The Senior Registry Data Analyst also provides leadership, mentoring, and training to Registry Data Analysts and other stakeholders while supporting strategic data initiatives and continuous process improvement.

Data Collection, Workflow Design & System Development

Lead collaborative stakeholders, including Coordinating Center staff and participating members, in the design and improvement of data collection workflows.
Evaluate database and website functionality and recommend enhancements to improve data capture, efficiency, and user experience.
Translate business and stakeholder requirements into technical specifications for database, reporting, and workflow solutions.
Design, develop, test, implement, and maintain database applications, web-based tools, and workflow enhancements.
Support data collection initiatives for quality improvement activities, research studies, and pilot projects.
Create and maintain training materials, documentation, and operational procedures.
Train and support over 100 internal and external users on database functions, reporting tools, and data collection processes.
Maintain detailed documentation of system functionality, report logic, and programming specifications.
Serve as a mentor and technical resource to team members and other data users.
Conduct site visits to hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and physician practices to evaluate workflows and identify opportunities for process improvements.
Function as the primary resource for troubleshooting database, workflow, and data collection issues.

Data Quality & Database Management

Develop and implement strategies to ensure data accuracy, consistency, completeness, and integrity.
Establish and maintain quality assurance processes for data collection and reporting.
Identify trends, anomalies, and potential data quality issues and implement corrective actions.
Manage database access, security, and user permissions in accordance with organizational policies.
Perform investigative data analyses to identify unusual data entry patterns and support auditing activities.
Recommend and lead data cleanup and validation initiatives.

Data Strategy, Analysis & Insights

Analyze structured and unstructured data to identify meaningful trends and actionable insights.
Collaborate with leadership and stakeholders to support strategic decision-making through data-driven recommendations.
Develop innovative approaches for leveraging data to achieve organizational goals.
Evaluate and implement new reporting tools, dashboards, and analytical methodologies.
Support recurring and ad hoc reporting needs across the collaborative.
Review data requests and ensure compliance with data governance standards and approved use policies.
Promote reproducible analytical practices through thorough documentation and quality control procedures.
Provide guidance to analysts regarding database structure, workflow considerations, and dataset interpretation.

Reporting & Website Management

Design, develop, and maintain updates to the collaborative's public-facing website.
Create reports, dashboards, and visualizations that effectively communicate performance metrics and quality improvement outcomes.
Present complex data in a format that is meaningful and accessible to diverse audiences.
Deliver scheduled and ad hoc reports to leadership, stakeholders, researchers, and collaborative members.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Health Services Administration, Healthcare Informatics, Computer Science, or a related field required.
Associate degree in Information Technology with six to eight years of directly related experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor's degree.

Experience

Five (5+) years of experience designing and implementing data collection systems for healthcare, research, or quality improvement initiatives.
Five (5+) years of SQL development and database management experience.
Five (5+) years of website development and maintenance experience.
Five (5+) years of project management experience.
Five (5+) years of experience with reporting and business intelligence tools.
Five (5+) years of healthcare-related experience.
Experience working with relational databases, data architecture, and data integration processes.

Additional Information

What We Offer

At Henry Ford Health, we foster an environment of collaboration, career growth, and mission-driven work. You'll have access to learning opportunities that empower you to make a meaningful impact in healthcare while working alongside dedicated professionals who share your passion for excellence.

Join Our Team

jobs.title: Project Manager, Operations (Agile)
jobs.description:
Job Summary:
The Project Manager, Operations (Agile) delivers a steady flow of short, high-impact operations projects for SUS Company 1, finishing them in weeks rather than months. Typical projects include line layout and changeover improvements, fixtures and small equipment, capacity quick-wins, scrap and yield fixes, 5S and visual management, pilot runs, new customer assemblies and reporting or system improvements. The role uses agile methods (short sprints, visual boards, daily stand-ups and quick feedback loops) to deliver working results early and adjust fast. It also builds change control, validation and documentation into each sprint, so that speed never comes at the expense of compliance under ISO 13485 and FDA requirements.

Responsibilities

Lead small cross-functional teams from Production, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, EHS and IT, often without direct authority.
Work with the Operations Leader as the product owner who sets priorities, and brings floor operators and supervisors into sprint reviews for fast feedback.
Coach teams and supervisors in agile and lean practices such as stand-ups, visual management, retrospectives and problem solving.
Manage vendors and contractors for small equipment, fixtures and installations, including quick quotes, purchase requests, installation and acceptance testing.
For larger projects (e.g., new cleanroom or production line, major equipment), use a hybrid approach: formal stage gates, business case and capital request (CapEx) at the top level, with agile sprints for design, build, test and validation work inside each phase.
Maintain an overall milestone plan and budget for these projects, and track cost and forecast-at-completion against the approved budget.
Hand over each result to operations with updated SOPs or work instructions, trained people and support in place.
Confirm benefits (e.g., capacity, savings, yield, cycle time) 30'90 days after go-live against the charter.
Capture lessons learned in every retrospective and improve templates, tools and the project process for Operations.
Report monthly on portfolio flow: projects completed, cycle times, benefits delivered and blockers.
Run a single intake process for operations project requests; screen each one for value, effort, urgency and compliance impact.
Scope each project on a one-page charter or A3 within 2'3 business days: problem, goal, measurable success criteria, scope limits, team, target finish date and change-control path.
Break larger ideas into small, independently valuable deliverables (for example: pilot on one line, then roll out to others) so results arrive early.
Keep a prioritized operations project backlog with the Operations Leader, re-ranked every 2 weeks based on business value, risk and capacity.
Use risk-based approval tiers so small, low-risk projects get quick sign-off, and reserve full stage-gate reviews for high-risk or high-cost work.
Plan work in 1'2 week sprints with clear sprint goals; hold sprint planning, 15-minute daily stand-ups at a visual board on the floor, sprint reviews and retrospectives.
Manage the project portfolio on a Kanban board (e.g., Backlog, Ready, In Progress, Validation/Documentation, Done) with work-in-progress limits so teams finish before they start new work.
Deliver a minimum viable result early (e.g., a trial fixture, temporary layout or pilot run), measure it, and improve it in the next sprint.
Remove blockers within 24'48 hours: secure decisions, parts, people and production time, and escalate quickly when needed.
Run rapid-improvement (kaizen) events of 3'5 days with production teams for focused problems.
Coordinate project work with Production Planning so trials, installations and cut-overs fit into planned downtime and protect customer deliveries.
Share progress openly with visual boards, burndown or cumulative flow charts and short weekly updates instead of long status reports.
Treat compliance as part of "done": a deliverable is only complete when its change control, validation, documentation and training are complete.
Screen each project at intake for impact on product, process, equipment, facility, software, customers or registrations, and choose the right change-control path early.
Plan validation (IQ/OQ/PQ, process and test method validation, computer system validation) with Quality and Validation from sprint one, and run documentation in parallel with the build, not after it.
Use pre-approved templates and standard protocols for repeat project types (e.g., fixtures, like-for-like equipment, layout changes) to shorten approval and validation time.
Keep project records audit-ready in line with ISO 13485:2016, FDA 21 CFR Part 820 (Quality Management System Regulation) and Good Documentation Practices.
Coordinate customer change notifications and regulatory assessments with Quality and Regulatory whenever a project could affect customer products.
Other Responsibilities as assigned

Why Bixal?

Bixal is a consulting company headquartered in Fairfax, VA, working alongside governments and organizations to help them deliver better services and experiences to the communities they serve. Using evidence-based knowledge and technology, Bixal empowers clients to deliver on their missions more effectively by fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement.

Our Values

People-First: Emphasizing the importance of people in all aspects of work.
Collaboration and Transparency: Valuing teamwork and open communication.
Growth Mindset: Encouraging innovation and continuous improvement.
Creating Lasting Impact: Focusing on meaningful outcomes and positive change.

About The Role

Bixal is seeking a Project Manager / Scrum Master (PM) to oversee contractor support for GSA’s Regulatory Information Service Center (RISC) systems, which federal agencies and OMB rely on to manage and publish regulatory information.

The PM will lead the day-to-day Operations & Maintenance (O&M) of the current legacy RISC systems and support their planned modernization. This role is responsible for task-level planning, coordination, and execution across all activities spanning development, infrastructure, security, help desk, communications, and training. The PM will ensure alignment with GSA objectives and support the agile delivery team to meet defined performance standards.

This is a full-time position contingent on contract award by our client, with a defined performance period of one year with two one-year option periods. This role offers you a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on a project that aligns with Bixal’s mission of delivering innovative, human-centered solutions. While the role has a fixed duration, we are committed to transparency and collaboration, keeping you informed about contract updates and new opportunities. At Bixal, we support your professional journey, ensuring your experience reflects our inclusive, purpose-driven culture and prepares you for future success.

Location 

This is a remote role. Candidates must be willing to travel to the Washington, D.C. area to conduct in-person meetings at government offices approximately once per quarter. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the US.  Bixal does not provide visa sponsorship.  

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $100,000 – $110,000. In the spirit of transparency, most offers tend to land near the midpoint of the range. We make compensation decisions thoughtfully, considering your experience, the skills you bring, and our commitment to internal equity. Fairness and transparency are core to how we operate.

Responsibilities

Manage the daily project activities for the agile development team, including schedule, scope, resources and support system operations and modernization efforts. Ensure activities align with established strategy, governance processes, and applicable standards while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
Supervise and manage contractor staff, provide technical guidance, and coordinate execution across multidisciplinary teams, including developers, help desk, training, infrastructure, and security.
Serve as the primary point of contact for government clients, including the Contracting Officer, COR, GSA product owners, and other government stakeholders.
Plan and lead project kickoff meetings to align the technical approach to the scope, schedule, roles, and expectations.
Lead agile planning, including backlog management, sprint and release planning, and reporting on planned, completed, and blocked work.
Develop and maintain the Project Management Plan (PMP), Quality Management Plan (QMP), Communication Plan, Change Management Plan, standard operating procedures, schedules, and task trackers to support transparent execution and progress monitoring. Develop and maintain roadmaps and modernization plans that show planned releases and the retirement of legacy functions.
Maintain Business Requirements Documents informed by ongoing process analysis, user research, technical discovery, and Government priorities.
Monitor progress and proactively identify, communicate, and resolve risks, issues, and dependencies. Prepare and deliver recurring project status updates and monthly reports summarizing activities, accomplishments, upcoming work, risks, issues, staffing, and budget.
Oversee release readiness, testing, and user acceptance testing to meet quality, accessibility, and security standards.
Manage transition-in and transition-out activities to ensure the continuity of services.
Track labor hours and funding against contract limits and support accurate invoicing.
Travel approximately quarterly to support in-person demonstrations, planning sessions, and collaboration sessions with client stakeholders.
Other relevant duties as assigned and qualified/trained to perform.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree, plus at least 4 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience serving as a Project Manager for digital- or web-focused initiatives in a large or complex organizational environment.
Expertise in activity planning, resource coordination, and schedule management.
Experience in managing O&M legacy systems and/or system modernization efforts.
Experience supervising staff and managing subcontractors.
Working knowledge of agile delivery practices (Scrum or similar), backlog management, and release planning.

Overview

Do you want to build an impactful career to change the world for the better?

Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for an experienced Environmental Remediation Project Manager – Geologist or Engineer
to join our Portland, Oregon office. This role is well-suited for a geologist, hydrogeologist, or engineer with consulting experience in the Pacific Northwest who has successfully led environmental investigation and remediation projects. In this position, your project leadership, client service, and technical expertise will be central to guiding complex contaminated site assessment and remediation work, including remedial investigations and feasibility studies, groundwater monitoring, soil vapor extraction, sediment and surface water sampling, technical reporting, and data-driven project delivery.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

This opportunity is especially well-suited for someone who enjoys combining field-based technical insight with project coordination, data evaluation, client service, and high-quality deliverables. You will have the opportunity to move beyond task execution into broader project ownership while continuing to contribute meaningfully to technical strategy and field implementation.

Task and project management, including planning and implementing investigation and remediation projects, budgeting and budget management, adherence to schedule, quality, client satisfaction, and profitability.
Evaluate contaminated sites and develop investigation and remediation approaches, including remedial investigations/feasibility studies, removal action work plans, remediation design plans, and remedy implementation under state and federal cleanup programs.
Lead proposal and work plan development, environmental data evaluation, conceptual site model updates, cost-benefit analyses, and technical recommendations that support practical cleanup strategies.
Implement and manage remedial pilot tests and systems, including soil vapor extraction, groundwater monitoring programs, vendor selection, logistical coordination, permitting, and supervision of field teams.
Write technical reports, letters, memoranda, plans, specifications, and proposals; oversee and review documents prepared by project teams.
Build and maintain strong relationships with both new and existing clients, using your expertise to support Geosyntec’s growth through effective business development and client management.
Foster trust-based relationships with clients, regulatory personnel, and other project stakeholders.
Mentor, guide, and motivate early career staff assigned in the areas of project performance, including technical tasks listed above, client expectations, and career development; work with employees to correct deficiencies.
At times, this position may also include fieldwork such as site visits, groundwater monitoring, surface and subsurface sediment sampling, surface water sampling, drilling oversight, contractor oversight, and remediation system operations, maintenance, and construction.
Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or a closely related discipline. (required)
Advanced degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or a related discipline. (preferred)
Professional registration (i.e., P.E. P.G.). (preferred)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At least 7 years (8+ years preferred) of direct environmental consulting experience in the Pacific Northwest marketplace; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Strong understanding of Pacific Northwest state and federal environmental regulations, with the ability to apply regulatory requirements to investigation, remediation, and closure strategies. (required)
Experience coordinating projects and tasks, including scope, schedule, budget, resource allocation, quality, technical oversight, subcontractor coordination, and financial tracking. (required)
Experience with remedial investigations, feasibility studies, groundwater monitoring, multi-media sampling methods and data acquisition, and environmental data analysis. (required)
Strong technical writing skills, including experience preparing work plans, RI/FS documents, monitoring reports, technical memoranda, proposals, and client-ready deliverables. (required)
Ability to mentor and coordinate early-career staff and field teams while maintaining strong communication with clients, regulators, subcontractors, and internal project teams. (required)
Ability to succeed in a fast-paced consulting environment, handling multiple project assignments, meeting strict deadlines, and traveling to client facilities as needed. (required)
Excellent writing and communication skills. (required)
Field work and overnight travel may be required.
Current OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER training and refreshers. (preferred)
Health & Safety training and medical monitoring. (required)
Client-driven drug and background testing may be required.
Valid U.S. driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)
