new_jobs.title: CQI Senior Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Henry Ford Health partners with millions of people on their health journey, across Michigan and around the world. We offer a full continuum of services from primary and preventative care to complex and specialty care, health insurance, a full suite of home health offerings, virtual care, pharmacy, eye care and other health care retail. With former Ascension southeast Michigan and Flint region locations now part of our team, Henry Ford's care is available in 13 hospitals and hundreds of ambulatory care locations. Based in Detroit, Henry Ford is one of the nation's most respected academic medical centers and is leading the Future of Health: Detroit, a $3 billion investment anchored by a reimagined Henry Ford academic healthcare campus.

Job Description

The CQI Senior Registry Data Analyst serves as a technical and operational leader responsible for the design, development, implementation, and optimization of registry databases, data collection systems, websites, reports, and workflows that support quality improvement initiatives across Michigan. Working with limited supervision, this role partners with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the collection of accurate, high-quality data that drives improvements in patient care and outcomes.

This position serves as the subject matter expert for registry data collection processes, database functionality, reporting, and workflow design. The Senior Registry Data Analyst also provides leadership, mentoring, and training to Registry Data Analysts and other stakeholders while supporting strategic data initiatives and continuous process improvement.

Data Collection, Workflow Design & System Development

Lead collaborative stakeholders, including Coordinating Center staff and participating members, in the design and improvement of data collection workflows.
Evaluate database and website functionality and recommend enhancements to improve data capture, efficiency, and user experience.
Translate business and stakeholder requirements into technical specifications for database, reporting, and workflow solutions.
Design, develop, test, implement, and maintain database applications, web-based tools, and workflow enhancements.
Support data collection initiatives for quality improvement activities, research studies, and pilot projects.
Create and maintain training materials, documentation, and operational procedures.
Train and support over 100 internal and external users on database functions, reporting tools, and data collection processes.
Maintain detailed documentation of system functionality, report logic, and programming specifications.
Serve as a mentor and technical resource to team members and other data users.
Conduct site visits to hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and physician practices to evaluate workflows and identify opportunities for process improvements.
Function as the primary resource for troubleshooting database, workflow, and data collection issues.

Data Quality & Database Management

Develop and implement strategies to ensure data accuracy, consistency, completeness, and integrity.
Establish and maintain quality assurance processes for data collection and reporting.
Identify trends, anomalies, and potential data quality issues and implement corrective actions.
Manage database access, security, and user permissions in accordance with organizational policies.
Perform investigative data analyses to identify unusual data entry patterns and support auditing activities.
Recommend and lead data cleanup and validation initiatives.

Data Strategy, Analysis & Insights

Analyze structured and unstructured data to identify meaningful trends and actionable insights.
Collaborate with leadership and stakeholders to support strategic decision-making through data-driven recommendations.
Develop innovative approaches for leveraging data to achieve organizational goals.
Evaluate and implement new reporting tools, dashboards, and analytical methodologies.
Support recurring and ad hoc reporting needs across the collaborative.
Review data requests and ensure compliance with data governance standards and approved use policies.
Promote reproducible analytical practices through thorough documentation and quality control procedures.
Provide guidance to analysts regarding database structure, workflow considerations, and dataset interpretation.

Reporting & Website Management

Design, develop, and maintain updates to the collaborative's public-facing website.
Create reports, dashboards, and visualizations that effectively communicate performance metrics and quality improvement outcomes.
Present complex data in a format that is meaningful and accessible to diverse audiences.
Deliver scheduled and ad hoc reports to leadership, stakeholders, researchers, and collaborative members.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Health Services Administration, Healthcare Informatics, Computer Science, or a related field required.
Associate degree in Information Technology with six to eight years of directly related experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor's degree.

Experience

Five (5+) years of experience designing and implementing data collection systems for healthcare, research, or quality improvement initiatives.
Five (5+) years of SQL development and database management experience.
Five (5+) years of website development and maintenance experience.
Five (5+) years of project management experience.
Five (5+) years of experience with reporting and business intelligence tools.
Five (5+) years of healthcare-related experience.
Experience working with relational databases, data architecture, and data integration processes.

Additional Information

What We Offer

At Henry Ford Health, we foster an environment of collaboration, career growth, and mission-driven work. You'll have access to learning opportunities that empower you to make a meaningful impact in healthcare while working alongside dedicated professionals who share your passion for excellence.

Join Our Team

Ready to make a difference? Apply now and be part of a team that's transforming healthcare.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Business Intelligence Analyst

The Center for Elders’ Independence is a PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the elderly) organization (PO) that uses an interdisciplinary team approach for care planning and implementing purposeful high quality, affordable, and integrated health care services to the elderly. Our elderly meet PACE requirements as prescribed by CMS and are referred to as participants. Our PO includes Adult Day Health Centers and primary care clinics, promoting participant autonomy, quality of life and the ability for individuals to live in their communities

THE POSITION: The Business Intelligence Analyst will support the Data & Analytics team by developing, maintaining, and optimizing enterprise reporting solutions— including SSRS, Power BI, and regulatory submissions. This role requires strong technical expertise, healthcare regulatory knowledge (CMS and State), and the ability to integrate and analyze data across fragmented clinical and operational systems such as Salesforce and eClinicalWorks ( eCW ). The analyst will play a key role in enhancing data governance practices and contributing to the creation of a unified data foundation.

The annual salary range for the Business Intelligence Analyst position at Center for Elders’ Independence is $95,721 to $145,496. Placement within the range is determined based on job-related factors such as relevant experience, skills, abilities, internal equity, and market data, consistent with CEI’s annual compensation review and established compensation practices.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop, maintain, and enhance SSRS and Power BI reports supporting leadership, operational, clinical, and regulatory needs.
Produce accurate, timely leadership, operational, and regulatory reporting deliverables.
Partner with stakeholders to define reporting requirements and deliver insights that support auditability and regulatory readiness.
Work extensively with data from Salesforce, eClinicalWorks ( eCW ), and Claim systems ; u nderstand and map data flows .
Perform data analysis to validate, cleanse, and reconcile data across disparate sources.
Business Intelligence Development
Design and develop new reports , and o ptimize existing reports / dashboards to improve usability, performance, and accuracy.
Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business needs into BI solutions.
Support data governance initiatives by contributing to data standards, definitions, and quality rules.
Help establish a unified data foundation and improve data reliability across the organization.
Work closely with data engineering to ensure consistent and accurate data ingestion.

QUALIFICATIONS:

7 + years of experience in Business Intelligence, Reporting, or Data Analytics.
Strong hands ‑ on experience with:
SQL Server / T ‑ SQL
SSRS
Power BI
Demonstrated expertise with healthcare reporting, especially:
CMS regulatory reporting
State-level medical/clinical reporting
Solid understanding of data integration, data modeling, and interoperability concepts.
Excellent analytical, problem ‑ solving, and communication skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience supporting data governance programs or enterprise data initiatives.
Familiarity with healthcare operational workflows and clinical terminology.
Background in a mission-driven or healthcare organization.

The above job description is intended to communicate the general function of the mentioned position and by no means shall be considered an exhaustive or complete outline of the specific tasks and functions that will be required. CEI reserves the right to change job descriptions, site assignments, and or work hours as required by the needs of the program. All employees are expected to perform their duties within their ability as required by the job and/or as requested by management.

Center for Elders’ Independence is a PACE (Program of All- Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization that uses an interdisciplinary team approach to care planning and care implementation for the purpose of providing high quality, affordable, integrated health care services to the elderly, including an Adult Day Health Center, and promoting autonomy, quality of life and the ability of individuals to live in their communities. Unlike other healthcare plans, CEI is not a "fee-for-service" plan. It is a “capitation” healthcare plan. CEI is paid a set amount for each person enrolled in our program, whether or not that individual seeks care. We are a growing company that offers stability and continues to thrive.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager, Operations (Agile)
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary:
The Project Manager, Operations (Agile) delivers a steady flow of short, high-impact operations projects for SUS Company 1, finishing them in weeks rather than months. Typical projects include line layout and changeover improvements, fixtures and small equipment, capacity quick-wins, scrap and yield fixes, 5S and visual management, pilot runs, new customer assemblies and reporting or system improvements. The role uses agile methods (short sprints, visual boards, daily stand-ups and quick feedback loops) to deliver working results early and adjust fast. It also builds change control, validation and documentation into each sprint, so that speed never comes at the expense of compliance under ISO 13485 and FDA requirements.

Responsibilities

Lead small cross-functional teams from Production, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, EHS and IT, often without direct authority.
Work with the Operations Leader as the product owner who sets priorities, and brings floor operators and supervisors into sprint reviews for fast feedback.
Coach teams and supervisors in agile and lean practices such as stand-ups, visual management, retrospectives and problem solving.
Manage vendors and contractors for small equipment, fixtures and installations, including quick quotes, purchase requests, installation and acceptance testing.
For larger projects (e.g., new cleanroom or production line, major equipment), use a hybrid approach: formal stage gates, business case and capital request (CapEx) at the top level, with agile sprints for design, build, test and validation work inside each phase.
Maintain an overall milestone plan and budget for these projects, and track cost and forecast-at-completion against the approved budget.
Hand over each result to operations with updated SOPs or work instructions, trained people and support in place.
Confirm benefits (e.g., capacity, savings, yield, cycle time) 30'90 days after go-live against the charter.
Capture lessons learned in every retrospective and improve templates, tools and the project process for Operations.
Report monthly on portfolio flow: projects completed, cycle times, benefits delivered and blockers.
Run a single intake process for operations project requests; screen each one for value, effort, urgency and compliance impact.
Scope each project on a one-page charter or A3 within 2'3 business days: problem, goal, measurable success criteria, scope limits, team, target finish date and change-control path.
Break larger ideas into small, independently valuable deliverables (for example: pilot on one line, then roll out to others) so results arrive early.
Keep a prioritized operations project backlog with the Operations Leader, re-ranked every 2 weeks based on business value, risk and capacity.
Use risk-based approval tiers so small, low-risk projects get quick sign-off, and reserve full stage-gate reviews for high-risk or high-cost work.
Plan work in 1'2 week sprints with clear sprint goals; hold sprint planning, 15-minute daily stand-ups at a visual board on the floor, sprint reviews and retrospectives.
Manage the project portfolio on a Kanban board (e.g., Backlog, Ready, In Progress, Validation/Documentation, Done) with work-in-progress limits so teams finish before they start new work.
Deliver a minimum viable result early (e.g., a trial fixture, temporary layout or pilot run), measure it, and improve it in the next sprint.
Remove blockers within 24'48 hours: secure decisions, parts, people and production time, and escalate quickly when needed.
Run rapid-improvement (kaizen) events of 3'5 days with production teams for focused problems.
Coordinate project work with Production Planning so trials, installations and cut-overs fit into planned downtime and protect customer deliveries.
Share progress openly with visual boards, burndown or cumulative flow charts and short weekly updates instead of long status reports.
Treat compliance as part of "done": a deliverable is only complete when its change control, validation, documentation and training are complete.
Screen each project at intake for impact on product, process, equipment, facility, software, customers or registrations, and choose the right change-control path early.
Plan validation (IQ/OQ/PQ, process and test method validation, computer system validation) with Quality and Validation from sprint one, and run documentation in parallel with the build, not after it.
Use pre-approved templates and standard protocols for repeat project types (e.g., fixtures, like-for-like equipment, layout changes) to shorten approval and validation time.
Keep project records audit-ready in line with ISO 13485:2016, FDA 21 CFR Part 820 (Quality Management System Regulation) and Good Documentation Practices.
Coordinate customer change notifications and regulatory assessments with Quality and Regulatory whenever a project could affect customer products.
Other Responsibilities as assigned
